summary: Radar for 2026-11-21, GLP-1 focus. Four things are driving search this week: (1) US Thanksgiving is on Nov 26, and US News, Men's Health and The Conversation all ran GLP-1 holiday guides on Nov 19–20. This is the peak window for holiday Shorts. (2) The class-wide FDA NAION label change (announced Nov 9) has reached mainstream news (ABC Nov 18) and legal and industry coverage (JD Supra, FoodNavigator Nov 20). That makes it a label-change search format, but it's already near its peak. (3) New approvals for the pill drugs: Health Canada approved Foundayo (Nov 13), Australia approved orforglipron, and the Wegovy pill (TGA Nov 2) is reaching AU pharmacies. Searches for 'foundayo' and 'wegovy pill' are rising in our CA and AU markets. (4) Fresh randomized data: retatrutide knee-OA (NEJM, Nov 8; still unapproved, so Shorts or chapters only), SURMOUNT-ADOLESCENTS (JAMA), the Penn semaglutide binge-eating RCT (ObesityWeek, Nov 17) and T-REx resistance training (still getting picked up: MarketWatch Nov 20, WaPo Nov 18). Following the playbook, long-form stays broad: Side Effects-style 'what to expect', Foundayo, Mounjaro vs Zepbound, the Zepbound vs Wegovy head-to-head, Serious Risks and Keeping Results. Narrow items go to Shorts. Rejected: employer and Medicaid coverage, the 'GLP-1 vacation' story, compounded and telehealth warning-letter stories, the psychosis-after-stopping case reports, FAERS aspiration (surgery is a banned topic), the kids aged 6–11 STEP Young trial (outside our audience and sensitive) and animal-stage pipeline press.

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide (Mounjaro, Zepbound) and the new NAION eye warning: what the label change says, how rare it is, and the symptoms to report right away
candidates.angle: A label-change explainer that stays calm and honest. FDA's class-wide requirement (Nov 9): across 126 RCTs, 6.4 vs 3.8 cases per 100,000 person-years. Then the one action: sudden, painless vision loss means contact your clinician now. Name NANOS and the AAO. Fits as a chapter in Serious Risks plus a Short. Don't make a standalone long video, since mainstream outlets have saturated it.
candidates.why_now: FDA announced Nov 9. ABC covered it Nov 18 and Denmark compensation stories ran Nov 19. JD Supra and FoodNavigator kept it in the news on Nov 20. Lawyers' claim content is flooding the topic, so a calm, label-based source is the gap.

candidates.topic: Foundayo (orforglipron) pill: what to expect, now approved in Canada and Australia
candidates.angle: An approved-drug search format, label only. Explain how a daily non-peptide pill differs from weekly tirzepatide. Label Trial 1: −11.1% on the top label dose (17.2 mg), in adults with obesity or overweight plus a weight-related condition, without diabetes. candidates.topic: Semaglutide and binge eating: the 60-week randomized trial (Penn, ObesityWeek Nov 17)
candidates.angle: A 'How GLP-1 works / food noise' angle. In a 60-week placebo-controlled RCT in adults with BMI over 27, semaglutide improved disordered-eating measures, and new eating-disorder symptoms were uncommon in both groups. It's semaglutide-only evidence, so the title is semaglutide-first. Not a treatment claim for binge-eating disorder (that's not an approved use). Signpost to a clinician. Best as a chapter in a food-noise video or a single Short.
candidates.why_now: Penn Today, News-Medical and PhillyVoice (Nov 18–19) plus the Int J Eat Disord paper. Few creators have covered it yet.
